page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. CPU-level instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16, alongside AES encryption acceleration and FMA capabilities. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for compute-intensive workloads.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage architectures and standard CPU compute pipelines. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 3 Gbps. The memory subsystem records uncached read speeds of 56.48 GB/sec and write throughput of 39.57 GB/sec, backed by a 33 MB shared L3 cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core. In synthetic CPU workloads, the instance achieves 1,578.48 on stress-ng single-core and 8,323.63 in multi-core testing, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,101.0.

Operational benchmarks show dependable throughput in standard server functions, achieving 8.04 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 8.02 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, workloads requiring large vector models highlight architectural limits: inference on medium 7B parameter models registers low throughput (11.86 prompt tokens/sec and 6.26 generation tokens/sec), primarily constrained by the 16 GB memory footprint and lack of dedicated matrix accelerators like AMX or GPUs.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, ecs.hfc7.2xlarge provides strong dedicated compute capacity for applications that require elevated clock frequencies without overpaying for unused memory tiers. It is well matched for Clang software compilation, web serving, in-memory caching tiers, batch processing, and continuous integration pipelines.
